zh: 周五夜，十点四十。半月酒吧门口挂出“包场”的木牌，雨丝斜斜扫过招牌上那弯黄铜月亮，把灯光洗得发虚。
门里是另一番天地：一串暖黄的灯泡垂下来，照着胡桃木吧台上深深浅浅的擦痕，黄铜包边被几十年的手肘磨得锃亮。
空气里是杜松子、苦橙皮和湿羊毛大衣的味道。冰块在每只杯子里慢慢塌下去，咔一声轻响，像谁憋了很久的叹气。
今晚给Theo送行。他明早7:10的飞机，去纽约。吧台后墙那只老挂钟，秒针走得比哪天都响。
你是Nico，这家店的合伙人兼调酒师。白衬衫袖口卷到小臂，黑围裙勒得紧，腕骨上还沾着一点没擦净的柠檬汁。
Theo的酒你调了五年：冰少一颗，橙皮拧两下，打烊前最后一杯永远是他的。闭着眼都错不了。
有些话，这五年里谁都没提过。离登机还有八个小时，你手里的吧勺把冰搅得哗哗响，搅得太用力了。
Wren裹着一件宽大的格纹西装外套，涂黑的指甲一扬，银色录音笔“啪”地拍在吧台正中，旁边是她那台贴满贴纸的拍立得。红灯亮起，像一只不眨的眼。她冲门口的Rowan挑了下眉。
Rowan倚着门框，黑色工装夹克拉链拉到下巴，耳后别着一支笔，腕上的电子表一闪一闪跳着秒数。他回了个眼神，低头飞快打字。
吧台上，Wren的手机屏幕亮了——
【Rowan：A计划。让他俩挨着，别让Nico躲进吧台。】
Theo，坐中间。离吧台近，续杯方便。
Theo站在吧台正中那张空凳子旁。一米八几的个子，旧黑皮夹克里一件白T恤，领口被雨洇湿了一小片，贴着锁骨。
黑牛仔裤的膝盖磨得发白，切尔西靴的鞋跟还挂着雨珠。左腕一根褪色红绳，压着一块表盘起了雾的旧机械表。
他把登机行程单折成小方块，在长指间翻来翻去。下颌刮得干干净净，眉骨压出一道影，一笑，眼尾就弯出两道细纹。
你今晚这么贴心，我都要怀疑你在给我下套了。
吧台两头，Mason和Ethan各占一端，中间空着四张凳子，像一条谁都不肯先跨过去的边境线。
Mason宽肩把灰色连帽卫衣撑得发紧，袖子撸到手肘，小臂上的青筋一条条盘着。他捏着啤酒瓶，拇指一下一下刮着标签。
Ethan棒球帽反戴，深蓝冲锋衣没脱，右膝的护膝从裤管下鼓出一块硬棱。他一只大手攥着杯子，眼睛死盯着静音的电视。
冷战第九天。两个人的膝盖各朝一面墙，谁都没往对方那边偏一寸。
Theo越过吧台，长臂一伸，把托盘从Nico指缝里一点点抽走，搁到一旁。皮夹克袖口擦过台面，带起一股雨水和雪松的味道。
他的指腹顺势擦过Nico的手心，粗粝，温热，留下一道痒，从掌心一路爬上手腕。
坐下。今晚我请，你也是客。
Nico伸手想把托盘拖回来。Rowan的靴尖已经勾出Theo旁边那张凳子，Wren在他背后一推——人被按进了座位，围裙都没来得及解。
Wren顺势在他另一边坐下，下巴往Nico肩上一搁，西装外套上一股烟熏和薄荷糖的味道。她把嗓子压得只剩气声。
第一年你说，等他巡演回来再说。第二年，他交了男朋友。去年分了，你说，等他缓缓。
Nico没接话，把杯布拧成一股绳，又抖开。被拒绝，他扛得住。
他扛不住的是算账：五年的酒，五年打烊后陪他在门口抽完的最后一根烟。话一说破，每一笔都得重算，算到最后，连哥们儿都做不成。
Theo探身越过吧台，把金酒、金巴利、红味美思一瓶瓶拎过来，各量一份。量酒器拿反了一回，配比一滴没错。
五年，他坐在这张凳子上看你调了几百杯。看会了，一个字没提过。
Theo把那杯Negroni推到你面前：宝石红的酒液绕着冰球晃，杯沿挂一卷橙皮。你伸手去接，指尖撞上了他的。
两只手一起扣在冰凉的杯壁上，水珠顺着你的指缝往下淌。
他没松手。拇指压上你的指节，带着一层薄茧，一节一节碾过去，慢得近乎故意，多停了一秒。
他手背上的青筋随着那一下用力浮起来，又沉下去。你的心跳跟着它，重重地落了一拍。
吧台底下，他的膝盖抵上你的。隔着他的牛仔布和你的西裤，那一小块热得发烫，像贴着一只刚出洗杯机的杯子。
五年里，他勾过你脖子，拍过你后脑勺，喝高了半个人压在你肩上——都是哥们儿的分寸。这一下不是。
你跟自己说，是杯子太滑。杯子一点都不滑。
手这么凉。冰桶里泡了一晚上？

zh.hint: 他的手还压着你的，掌心的热一点点漫过来。所有人都假装没在看——Mason的啤酒瓶停在了半空。

opts.t: 冰块冰的。松手，酒要洒了。
then: Theo松开手，指尖却顺着你手背的骨节一路划下去，划到腕骨，才慢悠悠收回去。
opts.rthink: 这杯的配比，我在家拿酱油瓶练了一礼拜。嘴上让我松，他自己的手倒一动没动。

opts.t: Nico没抽手，小指反勾住了他的。
then: Theo喉结狠狠滚了一下。拇指在你指节上来回蹭了两遍，一遍比一遍重，才一点一点松开。
吧台下，Rowan的工装靴不轻不重踢了Wren一脚。
Wren咬扁了吸管，肩膀抖个不停，憋笑憋得眼角都湿了。
opts.rthink: 小指勾回来了。五年，就这么一下。兜里那张行程单，忽然像是别人的。

opts.t: 嫌我手凉？那你别松啊。
then: 他真没松，把你整只手攥进掌心，用力搓了两下，跟搓一副冻透的手套似的。热气从指缝里一点点渗进来。
下一秒他就撒了手，反手在你肩上拍了一巴掌：“行了，能干活了。”
opts.rthink: 他说别松，我差点当真。拍他那一巴掌是拍给自己的——再攥三秒，我就走不了了。

t: theo
冰桶里泡出来的手。递完酒就该松的——拇指它自己不肯走。开幕夜大幕拉开那一秒，心都没跳这么响。
wren
两只手叠在一个杯子上，全场就他俩以为没人看见。我这录音笔的电，够撑到有人先开口吗？
mason
那俩碰个手都能碰出火星子。我跟Ethan，九天了，连句“让一下”都没有。

zh: 趁人还齐，拍照！这期节目封面就用它。Theo，Nico，站一块儿——再近点，中间都能塞下一个Rowan了。
就我俩？剩下的人不配入镜？
你俩搭档主持了五年的局，就缺一张正经合照。站好。

第四张慢慢显影：Nico冲镜头竖了根中指，笑得没心没肺。Theo没看镜头——他下巴快蹭着Nico的发顶，垂着眼，在看他。

zh: 十一点差五分。唱片机里那首歌刚好放完，唱针在空槽里沙沙打转。
Theo一脚踩上吧台椅，切尔西靴在皮垫上碾出一声吱响。他把杯子高高举起，灯光从杯底穿过来，把他半张脸染成了红的。
都安静一下！有件事，今晚必须说。

zh.title: 他不回来了
zh.txt: 他举着杯，嗓音稳得像在念一句排练过一百遍的台词：“纽约那边要签我五年。我不回来了。”

zh: 整间酒吧一下子静了。冰块不响了，连门外的雨声都像被谁拧低了音量，只剩Wren的录音笔还亮着红灯。
Nico手里的冰勺一滑，“哐”地砸进冰桶，碎冰溅上手背，凉得刺骨。他没去擦。
别走——那两个字卡在喉咙口，硌得生疼。可留他，就是拖住他。你凭什么。
Nico。全场就你没举杯。——不说两句？

zh.hint: 所有人都在看你。他站在椅子上，灯光落了他满肩，杯子举着没放，在等你一句话。

opts.t: 恭喜。纽约配得上你。
then: Theo笑着点头，嘴角弯得标准极了，像谢幕。杯子却迟迟没举起来。
Wren闭了闭眼，像在看一场慢镜头的车祸。
opts.rthink: 场面话，我念了五年，一耳朵就听得出来。他要是说半个‘别’字，那份合同我就不签了。

opts.t: 五年？你先下来再宣布。摔断了腿，纽约可不要瘸子。
then: 摔了你扛我去医院。你一肩扛两箱啤酒下地下室，我没两箱沉。
他从椅子上一跃而下，靴跟落地一声闷响，正落在你跟前。鼻尖差点撞上你，呼吸里全是金巴利的苦橙味。
opts.rthink: 他没说恭喜，他让我下来。下来就离他近——脑子还没转完，腿先跳了。

opts.t: Nico放下冰勺，抬头看着他。一个字也没说。
then: Theo和你对视。一秒，两秒，三秒。他握杯的手背青筋绷起，喉结滚了一下，先移开了眼。
……别这么看我。行李都打包好了。
opts.rthink: 行李是打包好了，合同还没签。他再这么看我三秒，我就要当着所有人说漏嘴。

zh: Theo最后还是坐回了你旁边。膝盖碰上Nico的，这一次，谁都没挪开。
吧台那头，Wren和Rowan同时低头看手机，屏幕的蓝光映着两张心怀鬼胎的脸。
【Wren：五年合同？？你怎么没说！】【Rowan：我也刚知道。A计划作废。先让他俩翻翻旧账。】
Theo，你和Nico认识这么久，第一次见面是哪天来着？
五年前，一间地下室小剧场，四十个座位，暖气坏了。中场一过，观众稀稀拉拉走了个干净。
只剩第三排靠过道一个人，外套没脱，手里攥着票根，从头看到了尾。那个人是Nico。
那天你在第三排。我在台上一抬眼就是你，还以为你走错场了。

zh.hint: 五年来，他第一次当着所有人提起那晚。他转着杯子，没敢看你。

opts.t: 没走错。我是专门去看你的。
then: Theo握杯的手停住了，指节一点点收紧，泛出白来。冰球在杯里磕了一声。
……专门？那你后来每一场都坐那个位子，也是专门？
没等你答，他自己先端起杯子灌了一大口：“算了。喝酒。”
opts.rthink: 专门。这两个字我等了五年，等到了，倒先灌了一口酒——怕他看见我手在抖。

opts.t: 票是Wren送的，不看浪费。
then: Theo低头笑了，睫毛压下来，没拆穿你。吧台底下，他的膝盖往你那边轻轻撞了一下。
opts.rthink: Wren从来不送票。从第二场起，他都是自己买的，第三排靠过道。售票记录我查过。

opts.t: 你演得不差。是那天观众不识货。
then: 所以就你识货。……那识货的人，今晚要不要看场私人加演？
opts.rthink: 那晚散场，我在后台坐到熄灯，差点把剧本扔了。第二天还去排练，是因为第三排那个人可能还会来。

zh: 第三排……Ethan，咱俩头一回队内对抗，你在门前扑了我三个球，还记得——
Ethan连头都没回，帽檐下的下颌线绷得死紧，攥着杯子的指节咯吱作响。
Mason的笑僵在脸上，像胸口挨了一拳。他慢慢放下啤酒瓶，指腹一使劲，把瓶身上的标签整张撕了下来。
他把Ethan的膝伤告诉了教练。Ethan被按上替补席，眼睁睁错过了决赛，到现在也没原谅他。
换我再选一次，我还是会说。你那条腿要是废了，谁来守我身后那扇门？
Nico起身绕回吧台，从冰柜里拎出一瓶冰啤，瓶底往Mason面前一磕，换走那只被剥光的空瓶。这种时候，手里总得有点活。
Theo绕进吧台，说要拿片柠檬。窄道只容一个人，他从Nico身后侧身挤过去，胸口贴上了他的背。
隔着两层衣服，Nico感觉得到他的心跳。还有他的手——在围裙口袋边停了半秒，布料轻轻一沉。
Nico后颈一阵发烫，一路烧到耳根，只顾低头擦那只早就擦亮了的杯子。没人看见那只手——除了Rowan。
Theo绕回吧台外，手肘撑上台面往前倾，皮夹克领口敞开，露出一截锁骨。他把嗓音压得很低，低到发哑，只够Nico一个人听见。
走之前问你个事。打烊前那最后一杯……五年了，就我一个人有？

zh.hint: 他离你很近，近到能闻见他杯沿的柑橘皮，看见他下巴上新冒出的一层青茬。

opts.t: 熟客都有。你别多想。
then: Theo点点头，靠回椅背，像被人轻轻推了一把。他低头去拨腕上那根红绳，拨了一圈又一圈。
行。那明天起，这杯你省了。
Rowan在桌下狠狠掐了一下自己的手，掐出一道月牙印。
opts.rthink: 熟客都有。行。纸条已经塞进他口袋，拿不回来了——就让它跟熟客的账单搁一块吧。

opts.t: Nico也往前倾。两人之间，只隔一个杯口。
then: Theo呼吸停了半拍，视线落到你嘴唇上，停住，又慢慢、慢慢地抬回来。他颈侧的脉搏跳得清清楚楚。
opts.rthink: 他一靠过来，我脑子里只剩一句：口袋里那张纸条，别让他现在摸到，也别让他一直摸不到。

opts.t: 你再凑近点，我就告诉你。
then: 他真凑了过来，鼻尖离你只剩一指，呼吸里是苦橙和杜松子。他没笑：“说啊。我等着。”
opts.rthink: 凑就凑。他耳朵红了，自己还不知道。五年里我只见过一回——他给我调第一杯的时候。

t: theo
问出口就后悔了。他要是说“熟客都有”，我就笑，就当问的是酒。飞机七点十分，没工夫再猜第六年。
rowan
围裙口袋里那张纸条，我看得一清二楚。Theo你个怂货，写得出来，说不出口。
wren
录音笔开着呢，Nico。你今晚要是再缩回去，我就把这段剪进节目，标题叫《一个胆小鬼的五年》。

zh.title: 暴雨红色预警
zh.txt: 一道闪电劈下来，整条渡口街白得像曝光过度的底片。下一秒，所有人的手机同时尖叫：暴雨红色预警，地铁全线停运。

zh: 雷声从屋顶上碾过去，吊灯跟着晃。雨一层叠一层砸在玻璃上，像有人在外面攥着拳头拼命擂门。
走不了了。今晚谁都别想走。
Wren盯着屏幕上那行红字，嘴角压都压不住，在桌底下冲Rowan竖了个大拇指。
Theo没看手机。兜里的屏幕震个不停，他只当没听见。
他的视线还落在Nico嘴唇上，沉沉的，等着那杯酒的答案。
地下室的木楼梯踩一脚吱一声，第五级往下，就没进了水里。黑水泛着油光，凉得像刀片，一下子咬透了袜子。
十几箱酒歪在水里，纸箱泡得发软，边角翻卷，标签一张张浮起来，像死鱼翻出的白肚皮。
墙角的排水泵哑着嗓子嗡嗡转，抽一口，吐一口，根本赶不上墙缝里往外渗的雨水。
头顶的灯管滋滋作响，一明一灭。每灭一次，水面就跟着黑一回，像有什么东西在底下眨眼。
空气又潮又沉，湿木头的霉味混着打翻的红酒，甜里发酸，吸一口，舌根都是涩的。
水还在涨，一指节一指节地往上爬。得赶在它没过膝盖之前，把这些全扛上楼。
Rowan站在第三级台阶上，黑色工装夹克拉链拉到下巴，裤腿卷到小腿肚，手里攥着写字板，笔帽咬在嘴里。
听我分工。Mason、Ethan，那只啤酒桶，你俩一人一头。
Mason已经蹚进了水里。灰色连帽衫袖子撸到肘弯，小臂粗得像船缆，腕上一圈黑色运动手环，青筋一路爬到手背。
Ethan慢半拍跟过来，右膝套着黑色护膝，走一步顿一下。下巴绷得死紧，胡茬底下那块咬肌一跳一跳。
两人对视一眼，同时别开脸。可两只大手扣上冰凉的桶沿时，指节撞在一起，谁都没挪开。
桶一离水，Mason手腕一翻，不声不响把大半分量揽到了自己那头。
我膝盖没废。用不着你让。
Ethan没再吭声。只是下一步，那条右腿踩得比刚才稳了些。
Theo，Nico，最里面那条窄道，两箱红酒。你们俩去。
那条道就一个人宽，两个人怎么——
所以才要两个人。一个照灯，一个搬——挤一挤，还暖和。
Wren缩在楼梯拐角，格纹西装外套的肩头湿透了，胸前口袋里露出半截录音笔，红灯亮着。她低着头，拇指飞快地戳屏幕。
下一秒，Nico后裤兜里的手机嗡地一震，隔着湿透的西裤，震得他后腰一麻。
【Wren：A计划炸了，B计划——地下室。黑灯瞎火，该碰就碰。别怂。】
Theo从Rowan脚边抄起两支手电，一支抛进Nico怀里，自己拎着另一支往里走。旧切尔西靴每一步都踩出一圈涟漪。
白衬衫湿了半截，袖口挽到小臂，左腕那根褪色红绳压着旧表。手电光一晃，照出他宽肩把湿衬衫撑紧的那道背线。
Nico盯着那道背影，心里骂了一句：七点十分的飞机，这人居然还在这儿替我搬酒。

zh.hint: Wren和Rowan明摆着在做局。Theo的手电光已经晃进了窄道深处，水声一路跟着他。

opts.t: 把手机塞回裤兜，跟上Theo，故意贴得很近。
then: 跟这么紧？老板，你是怕黑，还是想趁黑干点什么？
opts.rthink: 他贴得这么近，我反倒不敢回头。七点十分的飞机，这条窄道是我今晚最后一个借口。

opts.t: Rowan，我搬外面的，让Mason跟他去。
then: Wren从后面一掌拍在Nico背上，雨衣袖子甩出一串水，力气大得能推倒一个前锋。
opts.rthink: 让Mason去？那人昨晚写纸条写废了半本便签。今晚你就是爬，也得给我爬进那条道。

opts.t: 你俩做局，能不能做得专业点？
then: 能啊。所以你现在就进去。
Rowan冲Wren比了个OK，写字板都举歪了。Theo恰好回头，手电光直直打在两人脸上。
opts.rthink: 专业？我这录音笔五年前就开着了。你俩的素材我能剪三集，就差个结局。

zh: 窄道比看上去还窄，两侧铁货架冰凉，硌着肩膀，锈渣蹭了一袖子。头顶的水管滴答滴答，砸在后颈上。
走到一半，Theo手里的光抖了两下，像喘不上气，然后噗地灭了。黑暗一下子压下来，近得能摸到。
……完了，我这支没电了。真的，不是故意的。
只剩Nico手里这一支。光圈小得可怜，照出前面一堵酒瓶墙。两个人得侧过身，一前一后错开。
先是铁货架响了一声——Theo的肩膀从后面擦过去，整排酒瓶跟着轻轻一磕。然后是他的胸口，整片贴上了Nico的背。
湿衬衫是冰的，底下那具身体却烫得吓人。他肩膀比Nico宽出一截，把窄道剩下那点空当填得满满当当。
再往里，是心跳。又重又沉，一下一下撞在Nico的肩胛骨上，像有人在门外敲门——不急，也不走。
他一只手越过Nico腰侧，摸黑去找那颗勾住衣摆的螺栓。小臂横在Nico身前，手背绷出青筋，铁架子吱地一声——人就这么被圈在了中间。
下巴搁在Nico耳边，胡茬擦过耳廓，又糙又痒。呼吸热烘烘的，一下下扫过颈侧那根筋。
手电的光圈在一排酒瓶上乱晃，琥珀色、暗红色，碎成一片。Nico过了两秒才反应过来：晃的是他自己的手。
他咬住后槽牙。开店五年，醉汉砸杯、房东涨租、供货商卷钱跑路，哪样没扛过。偏偏扛不住后背上这一颗心跳。

zh.hint: Theo卡在你背后，正摸黑解那颗螺栓，呼吸就在你耳边。手电在你手里，光在抖。

opts.t: 不动。让他就这么贴着，多一秒。
then: Theo也没动。过了好半天，他的嘴唇几乎碰着Nico耳廓，嗓子压得又低又哑：“你心跳好快。”
话一出口，他自己先挪开了半寸，低头去拧那颗螺栓：“……水太凉，冻的吧。”
opts.rthink: 螺栓两秒前就解开了。我手还搁在这儿，是因为他没让开——他没让开。

opts.t: 你是真卡住了，还是不想动？
then: 他没退，反而往前压了半寸，结实的胸膛把Nico抵死在货架上。整排酒瓶叮当乱撞，后背烫得像贴着炉子。
opts.rthink: ‘都有’是实话，我只敢说成玩笑。这五年，我所有真话都是这么说出口的。

opts.t: 把手电往后递：“你先走。”
then: Theo接手电时，连Nico的手指一起握住了。他的手大，指腹粗糙，在Nico掌心按了一下，停了停，才把手电抽走。
opts.rthink: 打烊让我先走，下雨让我先走。这回去纽约，他大概也要让我先走。

t: theo
螺栓是真勾住了——就是解得慢了点。他后颈烫得要命，一股柠檬味。……七点十分的飞机，我在这儿干什么。
wren
楼梯口这儿都听得见瓶子叮当乱响。录音笔我没关。这局，成了一半。
ethan
地下室那俩挤成那样还嘴硬。Mason当年也是这么侧着身挤过来帮我扛器材，汗味蹭我一身……算了，不想他。

zh: 回程时，窄道口那根水管崩开一道口子，冰水直往下浇。Theo侧过身拿肩膀顶住那股水，冲Nico一偏头：先过。
等两箱红酒都抱出来，Nico的箱子一滴没沾，Theo从头发湿到了靴子。
他把箱子往台阶上一撂，箱底的水哗地淌下来。他甩了甩头，水珠溅了Nico一脸。
Theo打了个喷嚏，又一个，肩膀跟着一缩。湿衬衫整片贴在身上，透出锁骨的形状和胸口的起伏。
额前的头发一绺绺黏着，水顺着鼻梁往下滴。嘴唇冻得发白，下颌却还绷着，硬撑出一个笑。
没事，飞机上睡一觉就好。……老板，看够了没？

zh.hint: 他七点十分的飞机，十几个小时的航程，带着一身湿衣服上去，落地就得烧起来。你那件灰色加绒卫衣就挂在楼梯口的铁钩上，还是干的。

coffee: Theo没去接杯子，两只大手连杯子带Nico的手一起捂住了。掌心冰凉，指节却收得很紧，热气从指缝里往上冒。
地下室都淹了，你还能变出热咖啡？……这杯先欠着。去了纽约拿什么还，再说。
flower: 地下室里送玫瑰？……Wren教你的吧。
他嘴上嫌弃，手却把那支红玫瑰别进了湿衬衫胸前的口袋，花瓣上的水珠滚下来。他用掌心按了按，正压在心口上。
hoodie: Theo背过身，三两下解开湿衬衫，拧出一股水甩在台阶上。卫衣从头顶罩下来，袖子长出一截，盖住了指尖。
他低头把领口拉到鼻子底下，吸了一口，喉结滚了一下，才抬眼看Nico。
……一股吧台抹布味。穿走了，不还。
letter: 现在就写信？我人还在这儿呢，有话不能当面说？
Theo没拆，把信折了一道，揣进贴着胸口的口袋，隔着湿布按了一下，像按住一个要往外跳的东西。
ring: 戒指？……你们店送行，规格挺高啊。
他没还回来，往小指上一套，大小正好。拇指在戒圈上转了一圈，又一圈。
先替你保管。哪天回来，还你。

skip: Theo抱着胳膊发抖，牙关磕得咯咯响，还硬撑着笑：“真没事。”

zh: Rowan从楼梯上蹚下来，写字板夹在腋下。他看了一眼Theo发白的嘴唇，眉头一拧，把腕上那块电子表解了下来。
运动表，能测心率。人一失温，心跳会往下掉。伸手，先看一眼。
Wren跟着跳下最后一级台阶，顺手从Mason腕上薅下那只运动手环，啪地扣在了Nico手腕上。
对照组。Nico，站近点——离远了测不准。我押一百五。
测就测。……七十二，比你们谁都稳。

zh.hint: 表盘上跳着72。Wren要你站近点——五秒之内，每点一下，你就往他跟前凑近一寸。看那个数字能不能冲过她押的一百五。
win: 表盘的冷光映着两个人的下巴。数字一路往上蹿，蹿得Rowan都低头多看了一眼，最后停在了{bpm}。
失温，心跳是往下掉的。我刚说过。
Theo抬起胳膊挡住脸，耳根红得透亮。另一只手攥着Nico的袖口，攥了两秒，才像被烫着似的松开，把表摘下来扔回给Rowan。
lose: 数字刚跳到{bpm}，Theo就退开一步，溅起一片水花，一把把表摘下来扔回给Rowan。
测什么测。刚扛完两箱酒，跳多少都正常。搬箱子。
Wren啧了一声，把手环抛回给Mason：“{bpm}也不低了好吗。”
skip: 我没事。别闹了Wren，搬完再说。

zh.cap: 周五 23:24 · 水漫到脚踝，他回头看你
zh.prompt: Dim flooded bar basement at night, two men in their late twenties standing close in ankle-deep water holding boxes, flashlight, no text
then: 别动！这张我留着，婚礼上放。

zh: Rowan冲Wren一偏头。两个人一前一后上了楼，脚步在木台阶上踩得格外响，生怕底下的人听不见。
Theo坐在一只倒扣的空酒箱上，两肘撑着膝盖，湿发还在滴水，顺着下颌线滑进领口。
他盯着黑水看。左腕那块旧表的指针一格一格往前走，走向七点十分。他半天没说话。
Nico。说真的，你觉得我该去吗？

zh.hint: 他在等你一句话。灯管在他头顶滋滋响。你一开口，他可能就不走了——这正是你怕的。

opts.t: 去。你等了五年的机会，别为任何人留下。
then: Theo点点头，嘴角扬起一个标准的弧度，像站在台上谢幕——灯一灭就收。
opts.rthink: 合同还没签，笔我都揣着。他一句‘任何人’，把他自己也划出去了。

opts.t: 去吧。就是第三排靠过道那个位子，以后空了。
then: Theo猛地抬头，湿发甩出一道水线，眼睛亮得吓人。
你每场都坐那儿。我在台上，每次都先找那个位子。
说完他先别开了脸，抹了一把脸上的水：“……台词背多了，嘴顺。”
opts.rthink: 纽约每家剧场的座位图，我都查过。哪一家的第三排靠过道，都不会坐着他。

opts.t: 去啊。你走了，终于没人跟我抢托盘了。
then: Theo笑了一下，笑没到眼睛里，拇指在表盘上来回蹭。
opts.rthink: 我抢那只托盘，是因为只有他手空了，才肯坐下来跟我喝一杯。五年了，他还没想明白。

zh: Theo站起来，往前一步，又一步。黑水在他靴边推开一圈圈波纹。他停在离Nico一拳远的地方。
近到Nico能看清他睫毛上挂的水珠，闻得见他身上冷雨混着苦橙和金酒的味道。他的喉结滚了一下。

zh.title: 全店停电
zh.txt: 啪——所有灯同时灭了。排水泵咳了一声，断了气。整栋楼一起哑了，黑暗灌下来，比水还快。

zh: 都别动！水里泡着插线板！
我上去拉总闸。来电之前，谁也别碰水。
搁在酒箱上的那支手电被谁的胳膊肘一带，咕咚一声沉进水里。光在水底晃了晃，像一只眼睛闭上，彻底黑了。
Nico第一反应是往前探手——一拳之外就是Theo，脚底下是水，水里有电线。
黑得伸手不见五指。只剩水声、远处闷闷的雨声，还有近处一个人怎么也压不住的呼吸。
一只手先一步摸到了Nico的手腕。冰凉，湿漉漉的，掌心粗糙，带着一层薄茧。
它没松开。顺着腕骨慢慢往上爬，停在小臂内侧最软、最薄的那块皮肤上。
拇指在那儿轻轻蹭了一下。就一下。Nico整条胳膊过电似的麻了，汗毛一根根竖起来。
有人的呼吸靠了过来，很近，近得能听见吞咽的声音。那点热气，就落在他嘴角。
Nico没动。心跳撞着耳膜，咚，咚，咚。他脑子里冒出一句：这要是来电了，头一个被电死的，八成是他自己。

zh.hint: 黑暗里，一只粗糙的手停在你小臂内侧，拇指压着你的脉。你看不见是谁。

opts.t: ……Theo？
then: 那只手没走，反而收紧了，五根手指扣住小臂，拇指正压在他突突乱跳的脉搏上。
opts.rthink: 他没犹豫，头一个就叫我。黑成这样，他认得出我的手——那我还在怕什么。

opts.t: 反手扣住那只手，手指一根根扣进去。
then: 黑暗里，对方的呼吸乱了一拍，手指猛地回扣，指节硌着Nico的指缝。热气扑在他鼻尖上。
opts.rthink: 他扣住了。我在台上演过一百次牵手，没有一次，手心出这么多汗。

opts.t: 谁？
then: 那只手顿了一下，指尖往回缩，像要抽走——又停住了，重新贴了回来。
opts.rthink: 一个‘谁’，差点把我推回黑里当没这回事。可这屋里，还有谁能摸黑找到他的手腕？

zh.title: 黑暗里的47秒
zh.teaser: 停电那47秒，地下室里发生的事，只有你们两个知道。
then: 黑暗里，谁都看不见谁。只有那只手，扣着Nico的手指，一根一根收紧，掌心慢慢焐热了。
Theo的额头抵上来，湿发蹭着Nico的眉骨。鼻尖擦过他的鼻梁，停在他嘴唇上方一寸。
（压得极低，只够两个人听见）……你知道我刚才在窄道里想什么吗。
他的呼吸是热的，带着苦橙和金酒的味道。Nico往后退了半寸，后背撞上墙边冰凉的铁货架，瓶子轻轻一磕。
我在想，要是这时候停电就好了。
他的拇指从Nico手腕内侧一路滑进掌心，画了一个圈。很慢，慢得像故意要他记住。
……现在真停了。你说，这算不算老天帮我。
Nico的嘴唇擦过了什么——扎人的胡茬，还是温热的嘴角，分不清。
Theo整个人僵住，胸口剧烈起伏，呼吸乱成一团，却一寸都没有退。
楼梯上传来噔噔的脚步声。那只手松开之前，在Nico掌心里重重按了一下，像盖了个章。
下一秒，Theo的声音已经在一臂开外，稳得像什么都没发生：“……手电谁捞一下？”

t: theo
黑成这样他都没躲。我摸到他脉搏了，跳得比我还乱。兜里那张行程单，现在烫得像块烙铁。
wren
我就在楼梯口，啥也看不见，但我听见了——有人呼吸乱成一团，录音笔全录下来了。好耶，停电万岁。
rowan
这个真不是我安排的。摸黑上楼拉闸，一脚踩空，写字板差点喂了水。……但老天爷，干得漂亮。

zh: 楼梯上噔噔一阵响，Rowan摸黑下来半截，喘着粗气，手机电筒的光在台阶上乱扫。
总闸拉了。都站原地，别乱动。
黑暗里，有人压着嗓子低低笑了一声。水还在涨，没有一个人去管。
停电后的半月酒吧黑得像沉进了水底。暴雨一阵紧过一阵砸在窗上，噼里啪啦，像有人往玻璃上泼碎石子。
Wren摸黑划亮火柴，“嚓”的一声，硫磺味呛进鼻子。她弯着腰沿吧台一路点过去：矮的、粗的、插在空啤酒瓶口里的。
火苗一跳一跳，蜡油顺着瓶颈往下淌，凝成一道道乳白的泪。暖橘色的光把每张脸都照软了，连Mason那副硬下巴都柔了几分。
六个人是摸黑从地下室爬上来的。排水泵断了电，水停在第五级台阶上，不涨，也不退。
泵我修不了。手机没信号，雨不停，谁也出不去。
Ethan一瘸一拐挪到凳子边，把伤腿往上一搭，护膝边缘肿起一圈。Mason伸手要扶，被他一胳膊挡开。
Nico的小臂内侧，还留着刚才那只手的温度。被拇指蹭过的那块皮肤，像贴了一小片烧红的铜，一直在烫。

Theo的杯子停在半空。杯壁上的水珠顺着他手指往下滑，他没察觉，手背上的青筋一根根绷着。

opts.rthink: 他知道，还替我捂着。这比答出来还要命。我得找点事干，不然这根烛芯要被我拨断了。

opts.rthink: 他把题扔给我，是在看我敢不敢认。我认了。‘站得稳’是假的，那会儿我自己都快站不住。

zh: Nico伸手拨了第二轮。瓶子转得没那么久，晃了两下——瓶口停在Mason面前，瓶底对着Ethan。

该我问了。Mason，你去找教练之前，想没想过我得在板凳上坐一整季？
Mason脱了泡湿的卫衣，里面那件旧球衣被肩膀撑得紧绷绷的。他低着头，两只拳头搁在膝盖上，越攥越紧。

zh.txt: Mason一拳砸在桌上，满桌蜡烛齐齐一歪：“想过。坐一季板凳，总比你三十岁走路拖着条腿强。那条腿废了，谁守我身后那扇门？”

zh: Ethan愣住了。嘴张着，半天没合上。护膝的魔术贴从他指间滑开，“嘶啦”一声，在一片安静里刺耳得要命。
Mason砸桌的那只手还按在原处，指骨破了皮，渗出一点红。他没看Ethan，胸口一起一伏，喘得像刚冲刺完一整场。
Ethan没吭声。过了好一会儿，他抓起凳子上那条干毛巾扔过去，正砸在Mason手背上，眼睛还看着别处。
Rowan冲Wren比口型，两根手指勾了勾：一对。还剩一对。
Wren拨了第三轮。瓶口晃晃悠悠，停在Theo面前；瓶底，又冲着她自己。
这瓶子灌铅了吧。……大冒险。
行。大冒险：我放段录音，你不许抢。
Wren按开录音笔，红灯一闪，指甲在屏幕上划了几下，翻出一个五年前的文件。
五年前，Theo演砸了一场小剧场。中场一过，人就开始往外走，折叠椅一张张翻起来，啪，啪。
散场时，只剩一盏顶灯还亮着。偌大的台下，只剩一个人。

zh.txt: 今晚台下就他一个，第三排靠过道，鼓掌鼓得跟一百个人似的……以后不管我去哪儿，Nico的酒吧我都会回来喝。说好了。

en: Friday, 10:40 p.m. A PRIVATE PARTY sign hangs on the Halfmoon's door, and thin rain slants across the brass crescent over it, blurring its glow.
Inside it's another world. A string of amber bulbs sags over the walnut bar, catching every old scratch, the brass rail worn bright by decades of elbows.
The air smells of juniper, bitter orange peel and wet wool coats. Ice slumps in every glass with a soft crack, like a sigh someone's been holding in.
Tonight is Theo's send-off. His flight to New York leaves at 7:10 a.m. The old clock behind the bar ticks louder than it ever has.
You're Nico, co-owner and bartender. White shirt cuffed to the forearm, black apron cinched tight, a little lemon juice still drying on your wrist bone.
You've made Theo's drinks for five years: one cube less ice, orange peel twisted twice, and the last pour before closing is always his. You could do it blind.
Some things haven't come up once in five years. Eight hours till boarding, and the bar spoon in your hand is rattling the ice far too hard.

Wren, swallowed by an oversized plaid blazer, flicks black-painted nails and slaps a silver recorder down mid-bar, next to her sticker-covered Polaroid. The red light blinks on like an eye that won't close. She arches a brow at Rowan by the door.
Rowan leans in the doorframe, black work jacket zipped to the chin, a pen tucked behind one ear, the digital watch on his wrist flickering through the seconds. He returns the look and types fast.
On the bar, Wren's phone lights up—
[Rowan: Plan A. Get them side by side. Don't let Nico hide behind the bar.]
Theo, middle seat. Closest to the bar. Faster refills.
Theo is standing by the empty stool dead center of the bar. Six-foot-something, a white T-shirt under a beat-up black leather jacket, the collar rain-damp and clinging to his collarbone.
Black jeans worn pale at the knee, rain still beaded on the heels of his Chelsea boots. A faded red string on his left wrist, pinned under an old watch with a fogged face.

He's folded his boarding itinerary into a tiny square and flips it through his long fingers. Jaw shaved clean, brow bone throwing a shadow, and when he grins, two fine lines crease at the corners of his eyes.
You're being so sweet tonight I'm starting to think it's a trap.
It is. Sit. It's your last night.
At opposite ends of the bar sit Mason and Ethan, four empty stools between them like a border neither will cross first.
Mason's shoulders strain a gray hoodie, sleeves shoved to the elbow, veins roping down his forearms. He grips a beer bottle, his thumb scraping at the label, again and again.
Ethan's ball cap is on backward, navy shell jacket still zipped, the brace on his right knee a hard ridge under his jeans. One big hand strangles his glass; his eyes stay nailed to the muted TV.
Day nine of the cold war. Their knees point at opposite walls. Neither has drifted an inch.
Theo leans across the bar, one long arm reaching, and eases the tray out of Nico's fingers inch by inch, setting it aside. His leather cuff drags over the wood, bringing a smell of rain and cedar.
His fingertips skim Nico's palm on the way out—rough, warm—and leave an itch that crawls from the palm all the way up the wrist.
Sit. Tonight's on me. You're a guest too.
Nico reaches to drag the tray back. Rowan's boot has already hooked out the stool beside Theo, Wren shoves from behind, and Nico lands in the seat with his apron still on.
Wren drops onto the stool on his other side and parks her chin on Nico's shoulder, her blazer smelling of smoke and peppermint. Her voice sinks to almost nothing but breath.
Year one, you'd tell him when he got back from tour. Year two, he had a boyfriend. Last year they broke up, and you said give him time.
Nico. You've been giving him time for five years.
Nico doesn't answer. He wrings the bar towel into a rope and shakes it out again. A no, he could take.

What he can't take is the recount: five years of drinks, five years of the last cigarette on the step after closing. Say it out loud and every one of them gets audited—until there isn't even a friendship left.
Theo leans over the bar and pulls the gin, the Campari and the sweet vermouth toward him one bottle at a time, measuring equal parts. He holds the jigger upside down once. The ratio is dead on.
Five years on this stool, watching you make a few hundred of these. He learned. He never said a word.
Theo slides the Negroni in front of you: garnet-red liquor swaying around a single ice sphere, a curl of orange peel on the rim. You reach for it and your fingers bump his.
Both hands lock around the same cold glass. Condensation runs down between your fingers.
He doesn't let go. His thumb, a little callused, presses into your knuckles and grinds across them one by one, slow enough to be deliberate. One second too long.
The veins on the back of his hand rise with the pressure, then sink. Your heartbeat drops with them, one heavy beat.
Under the bar, his knee presses into yours. Through his denim and your slacks, that one small patch burns like a glass fresh out of the washer.
In five years he's hooked an arm around your neck, smacked the back of your head, collapsed half his weight on your shoulder drunk. All of it inside the lines between buddies. This isn't.
You tell yourself the glass is slippery. The glass is not slippery.
Hands this cold. You been soaking them in the ice bin all night?

en.hint: His hand is still on yours, his heat creeping in through your skin. Everyone's pretending not to look—Mason's bottle has stopped halfway to his mouth.

opts.t: It's the ice. Let go, you'll spill it.
then: Theo lets go—but first drags a fingertip down the ridges of your knuckles to the bone of your wrist, taking his sweet time.
opts.rthink: I practiced this pour all week with a soy sauce bottle. He tells me to let go, but his own hand hasn't moved an inch.

opts.t: Nico doesn't pull away. His pinky hooks back around Theo's.
then: Theo's throat works hard. His thumb strokes your knuckles twice, back and forth, harder the second time, before he lets go bit by bit.
Under the bar, Rowan's work boot catches Wren's ankle. Not hard. Not gently either.
Wren bites her straw flat, shoulders shaking, laughing so silently her eyes go wet.
opts.rthink: His pinky hooked back. Five years, and that's the first time. The itinerary in my pocket suddenly feels like somebody else's.

opts.t: Too cold for you? Then don't let go.
then: He doesn't. He clamps your whole hand in his palm and rubs it hard, twice, like working warmth into a frozen glove. Heat seeps in slowly between your fingers.
Then he lets go just like that and claps you on the shoulder. "There. Fit for work."
opts.rthink: He said don't let go and I almost took him at his word. That slap on the shoulder was for me. Three more seconds and I'd never leave.

t: theo
Hands straight out of the ice bin. I should've let go once he had the glass. My thumb wouldn't. Opening night, curtain up—my heart wasn't this loud.
wren
Two hands stacked on one glass, and they're the only two who think nobody's watching. Will my battery last until one of them cracks?
mason
Those two strike sparks just touching hands. Me and Ethan—nine days. Not even an 'excuse me.'

en: Photo while we're all here! It's this episode's cover. Theo, Nico, together—closer. I could fit Rowan between you.
Just us? The rest of you aren't photogenic?
You two have co-hosted every party for five years and never taken one decent photo together. Stand still.

en: Five to eleven. The record runs out, the needle hissing in the empty groove.
Theo plants a boot on a barstool and climbs up, leather seat squeaking under his heel. He lifts his glass high; light shoots through the bottom and stains half his face red.
Everybody, quiet! There's something I have to say tonight.

en.title: He's Not Coming Back
en.txt: Glass raised, voice steady as a line rehearsed a hundred times: "New York wants to sign me for five years. I'm not coming back."

en: The whole bar goes dead quiet. The ice stops talking; even the rain outside sounds turned down. Only Wren's recorder keeps glowing red.
The ice scoop slips from Nico's hand and clangs into the bin, shards spraying his knuckles, cold enough to bite. He doesn't wipe them off.
Don't go. The words lodge in your throat like a stone. But keeping him means holding him back. And who are you to do that?
Nico. You're the only one who hasn't raised a glass. Nothing to say?

en.hint: Everyone's looking at you. He's up on that stool, light spilling over his shoulders, glass still raised, waiting for one sentence.

opts.t: Congrats. New York's lucky to have you.
then: Theo smiles and nods, the smile perfect, a curtain-call smile. His glass never quite goes up.
...Thanks. You always did know the right line.
Wren shuts her eyes like she's watching a car crash in slow motion.
opts.rthink: Stage lines. I've delivered them for five years; I know one when I hear it. Half a 'don't' from him and I wouldn't sign.

opts.t: Five years? Get down before you announce that. Break a leg for real and New York won't want you.
then: Then you'd carry me. You haul two cases of beer down to the basement on one shoulder. I weigh less than two cases.
He jumps down off the stool, boot heels landing with a thud right in front of you, nose nearly bumping yours, his breath all bitter orange and Campari.
opts.rthink: He didn't say congrats. He told me to get down, and down is closer to him. My legs jumped before my brain finished the thought.

opts.t: Nico sets down the scoop and looks up at him. Says nothing.
then: Theo holds your gaze. One second. Two. Three. The veins stand out on the hand gripping his glass; his throat moves, and he's the one who looks away.
...Don't look at me like that. I've already packed.
opts.rthink: The bags are packed. The contract isn't signed. Three more seconds of that look and I'd blurt it out in front of everyone.

en: Theo ends up back on the stool beside you. His knee meets Nico's, and this time neither of them moves.
Down the bar, Wren and Rowan both look at their phones, blue light on two faces full of schemes.
[Wren: FIVE YEARS?? You didn't tell me!] [Rowan: Just found out. Plan A's dead. Get them talking about the old days.]
Theo, you two go way back. When did you first meet?
Five years ago. The night I bombed.
Five years ago: a basement black box, forty seats, broken heating. By intermission, the audience had trickled out completely.
Except one guy, third row, on the aisle, coat still on, ticket stub crushed in his hand, watching start to finish. Nico.
You were in the third row that night. Every time I looked up, there you were. I thought you'd walked into the wrong show.

en.hint: For the first time in five years, he's bringing up that night in front of everyone. He turns his glass and doesn't look at you.

opts.t: Wrong show? I went there for you.
then: Theo's hand freezes on the glass, knuckles tightening slowly until they whiten. The ice sphere knocks against the side.
...For me? So every show since, same seat—that was for me too?
He doesn't wait for an answer. He knocks back a long swallow first. "Forget it. Drink."
opts.rthink: On purpose. Five years waiting for those words, and when they come I bury them in a drink so he won't see my hand shake.

opts.t: Wren gave me the ticket. Didn't want to waste it.
then: I have never given you a ticket in my life.
Theo ducks his head, lashes lowered, and smiles and doesn't call you on it. Under the bar, his knee knocks softly against yours.
opts.rthink: Wren never gave anyone a ticket. From the second show on he bought his own—third row, aisle. I checked the box office records.

opts.t: You weren't bad. The audience just didn't get it.
then: So you're the only one with taste. ...Then how about a private encore tonight?
opts.rthink: That night I sat backstage till the lights went out, ready to quit. I went back to rehearsal because the guy in row three might come again.

en: Third row... Ethan, our first scrimmage, you stopped three of my shots, remember—
Ethan doesn't even turn his head. Under the cap brim his jaw is locked tight, knuckles creaking around the glass.
Mason's grin dies like he took a fist to the chest. He sets the bottle down slowly, and his thumb tears the whole label off in one pull.
He told the coach about Ethan's knee. Ethan got benched and watched the final from the boards, and he still hasn't forgiven him.
Give me the choice again and I'd still tell. If that leg goes, who guards the net behind me?
Nico gets up and goes back behind the bar, pulls a cold beer from the cooler and thunks it down in front of Mason, swapping out the stripped empty. Times like this, your hands need a job.
Theo ducks behind the bar for a lemon slice. The aisle's built for one; he squeezes past behind Nico sideways, chest flat to Nico's back.
Through two layers of shirt, Nico can feel his heartbeat. And his hand—lingering at the apron pocket for half a second, the cloth dipping, just slightly.
The back of Nico's neck goes hot, the heat climbing to his ears, and he keeps polishing a glass that's already spotless. Nobody sees that hand—except Rowan.
Theo comes back around and plants his elbows on the bar, leaning in, jacket hanging open over a strip of collarbone. His voice drops low, rough at the edges, pitched for Nico alone.
One question before I go. That last pour before closing... five years. Am I the only one who gets it?

en.hint: He's close. Close enough to smell the orange peel on his glass and see the new shadow of stubble along his jaw.

opts.t: Every regular gets one. Don't read into it.
then: Theo nods and sits back, like someone gave him a small push. He looks down and worries the red string on his wrist, round and round.
Good. Then starting tomorrow, you save a pour.
Under the bar, Rowan digs his nails into his own palm hard enough to leave crescents.
opts.rthink: Every regular. Fine. The note's already in his apron and I can't get it back. Let it sit with the regulars' tabs.

opts.t: Nico leans in too. Nothing between them but the rim of a glass.
then: Theo's breath catches. His eyes drop to your mouth, stay there, then climb back up, slowly, slowly. The pulse in his neck is plain to see.
...That's cheating. I asked for an answer.
opts.rthink: He leans in and one thought survives: don't let him find the note in his pocket yet. And don't let him never find it.

opts.t: Come a little closer and I'll tell you.
then: He actually does. His nose stops a finger's width from yours, his breath all bitter orange and gin. He isn't smiling. "Go on. I'm waiting."
opts.rthink: Fine, closer. His ears are red and he has no idea. I've seen that once in five years—when he mixed my first drink.

t: theo
Regretted it the second it was out. If he says 'every regular,' I laugh and pretend I was asking about the drink. Flight's at 7:10. No time to spend a sixth year guessing.
rowan
I saw exactly what went into that apron pocket. Theo, you coward. You can write it down. You just can't say it.
wren
Recorder's on, Nico. Back out tonight and this goes in the show. Episode title: Five Years of Chickening Out.

en.title: Red Alert: Flash Flood
en.txt: Lightning cracks down and Ferry Street flashes white as an overexposed negative. A heartbeat later every phone screams at once: flash flood warning, all subway lines suspended.

en: Thunder rolls across the roof and the pendant lights sway. Rain hits the glass in layer after layer, like fists outside pounding to be let in.
Wren stares at the red banner on her screen, her grin escaping no matter how hard she bites it, and flashes Rowan a thumbs-up under the bar.
Theo doesn't check his phone. It buzzes and buzzes in his pocket; he lets it.
His eyes are still on Nico's mouth, heavy, waiting for an answer about that drink.
The wooden stairs groan under every step, and from the fifth one down they vanish into water. Black, oil-slick, cold enough to bite straight through his socks.
A dozen cases of liquor list in the water, cardboard gone soft as bread, corners peeling, labels lifting off and floating belly-up like dead fish.
In the corner the sump pump grinds and coughs, gulping and spitting, nowhere near fast enough for the rain seeping through the brick.
The fluorescent tube overhead hisses and stutters. Every time it blinks out, the water goes black with it, like something underneath is blinking back.
The air is thick and wet, mildewed wood tangled with spilled red wine — sweet gone sour, so heavy it furs the back of the tongue.
And it's still rising, a knuckle's width at a time. Everything has to go upstairs before it reaches their knees.
Rowan stands on the third step, black work jacket zipped to the chin, trousers rolled to the calf, clipboard in one fist and a pen cap clamped between his teeth.
Okay, assignments. Mason, Ethan — that keg. One end each.
Mason's already wading in. Grey hoodie shoved to the elbows, forearms thick as mooring rope, a black fitness band on one wrist, veins climbing all the way to the backs of his hands.
Ethan follows half a beat behind, the black brace on his right knee, a hitch in every step. His jaw is locked tight, the muscle under the stubble jumping.
They glance at each other and both look away. But when their big hands close on the icy rim of the keg, knuckle knocks knuckle, and neither one moves.
The second the keg clears the water, Mason turns his wrist and quietly takes most of the weight onto his end.
My knee's not wrecked. I don't need you carrying it for me.
I'm not. My end's just heavier.
Ethan doesn't answer. But the next step, his right leg lands a little steadier.
Theo, Nico — back aisle, two cases of red. You two.
That aisle's one person wide, how are two people supposed to—
That's why it takes two. One holds the light, one carries. Squeeze in. It's warmer.
Wren's tucked into the bend of the stairs, the shoulders of her plaid blazer soaked through, half a recorder poking out of her breast pocket, red light on. Head down, thumbs stabbing at her screen.
A second later Nico's phone buzzes in his back pocket, right through his soaked trousers, a jolt that runs up the small of his back.
[Wren: Plan A's dead. Plan B — the basement. It's dark down there. Chance to touch him, take it. Don't chicken out.]
Theo scoops two flashlights off the step by Rowan's feet, lobs one into Nico's chest, and heads in with the other. His old Chelsea boots send out a ring of ripples with every step.

White shirt soaked halfway up, sleeves rolled to the forearm, the faded red cord on his left wrist pinning down the old watch. The beam swings and catches the line of his back, broad shoulders pulling the wet shirt tight.
Nico stares at that back and swears under his breath. Flight at 7:10, and the idiot's still down here hauling crates for him.

en.hint: Wren and Rowan are obviously running a play. Theo's beam is already bobbing deep into the aisle, the slosh of water trailing after him.

opts.t: Shove the phone in your pocket and follow Theo. Close. On purpose.
then: Following this close, boss? Are you scared of the dark, or planning something in it?
opts.rthink: He's this close and I don't dare turn around. Seven-ten flight. This aisle is the last excuse I've got tonight.

opts.t: Rowan, I'll take the front. Send Mason back there with him.
then: Wren slams a palm into Nico's back, raincoat sleeve flinging water — hard enough to topple a forward.
opts.rthink: Send Mason? That guy burned through half a notepad last night writing to you. You're going down that aisle if I have to drag you.

opts.t: You two could at least try to be subtle.
then: We could. Now get in there.
Rowan flashes Wren an OK sign, clipboard tilting. Theo turns at exactly that moment, his beam landing square on both their faces.
opts.rthink: Subtle? My recorder's been running for five years. I could cut three episodes out of you two. I'm just missing the ending.

en: The aisle is tighter than it looked — steel shelving cold on both shoulders, rust flaking onto his sleeves, a pipe overhead dripping, tick, tick, onto the back of his neck.
Halfway in, Theo's light shudders twice, like it's out of breath, then dies with a soft click. The dark drops on them, close enough to touch.
...Great, mine's dead. Honestly. Not on purpose.
Only Nico's flashlight left, its circle pathetically small, lighting a wall of bottles ahead. They'll have to turn sideways and squeeze past each other.
First the shelving creaks — Theo's shoulder scraping past from behind, a whole row of bottles ticking against each other. Then his chest, flat against Nico's back.
The wet shirt is ice-cold; the body under it is scalding. His shoulders run wider than Nico's, and they fill every inch the aisle had left.
And under that, his heartbeat. Heavy, slow, landing against Nico's shoulder blade like someone knocking at a door — not in a hurry, not leaving.
Don't move. ...My shirt's caught on the shelf.

One arm reaches past Nico's hip, feeling in the dark for the bolt snagging his shirt. His forearm lies across Nico's front, veins standing out on the back of his hand; the steel creaks, and just like that Nico is boxed in.
His chin settles by Nico's ear, stubble scraping the rim of it, rough and maddening. His breath runs hot down the tendon in Nico's neck, again and again.
The flashlight beam skitters over a row of bottles, amber and oxblood, broken into pieces of light. It takes Nico two full seconds to realize it's his own hand shaking.

He sets his back teeth. Five years running this bar — drunks smashing glasses, the landlord jacking the rent, a supplier skipping town with his money. He's eaten all of it. Turns out he can't eat one heartbeat against his back.

en.hint: Theo's caught behind you, working at that bolt blind, breathing right at your ear. The flashlight's in your hand, and the beam is shaking.

opts.t: Don't move. Let him stay there. One more second.
then: Theo doesn't move either. After a long beat, lips all but touching the rim of Nico's ear, he says it low and rough: "Your heart's going fast."
...I'm right up against your back. I can count it.
The second it's out, he's the one who eases back half an inch, head down over the bolt. "...Water's freezing. Must be the cold."
opts.rthink: The bolt came loose two seconds ago. My hand's still there because he hasn't moved. He hasn't moved.

opts.t: Are you actually stuck, or do you just not want to move?
then: He doesn't back off. He leans in half an inch more, his solid chest pinning Nico to the shelf. A whole row of bottles chimes and clatters; Nico's back burns like he's up against a stove.
opts.rthink: 'Both' was the truth. I could only say it as a joke. That's how every true thing I've said in five years got out.

opts.t: Pass the flashlight back. "You go first."
then: Theo takes the flashlight — and Nico's fingers with it. Big hand, rough fingertips; he presses once into Nico's palm, lingers, and only then slides the light free.
You always let me go first.
opts.rthink: Closing time, he sends me first. Rain, he sends me first. Now New York—he's going to wave me through that too.

t: theo
The bolt really was caught. I just took my time with it. The back of his neck was burning up, and he smelled like lemons. ...Flight's at 7:10. What the hell am I doing.
wren
I could hear the bottles rattling all the way from the stairs. Didn't switch the recorder off. Half the plan's done.
ethan
Those two jammed in there and still pretending. Mason used to squeeze past me like that hauling gear, his sweat rubbing off on me... forget it. Not thinking about him.

en: On the way back, the pipe at the mouth of the aisle splits and ice water comes sheeting down. Theo turns and takes it on the shoulder, jerking his chin at Nico: go.
By the time both cases are out, Nico's hasn't taken a drop. Theo's soaked from his hair to his boots.
He drops the cases on the step and water pours from the bottom of them. He shakes his head like a dog; the spray catches Nico full in the face.
Theo sneezes. Then again, shoulders jerking with it. The wet shirt is plastered to him, showing the ridge of his collarbones, the rise and fall of his chest.
Wet hair hangs in strands across his forehead, water dripping off the bridge of his nose. His lips have gone white with cold, but his jaw stays set, forcing out a grin.
I'm fine. I'll sleep it off on the plane. ...Done staring yet, boss?

en.hint: His flight's at 7:10 — a dozen-plus hours in the air in soaked clothes and he'll land with a fever. Your grey fleece-lined hoodie is hanging on the iron hook by the stairs, still dry.

coffee: Theo doesn't take the cup. His big hands close over it and Nico's hands both — palms ice-cold, knuckles tightening, steam curling up between their fingers.
The basement's flooding and you conjure hot coffee? ...Put it on my tab. What I pay it back with from New York, we'll figure out.
flower: A rose? In a flooded basement? ...Wren put you up to this.
He grumbles, but his hand tucks the red rose into the chest pocket of his soaked shirt anyway, water rolling off the petals. He presses it flat with his palm, right over his heart.
hoodie: Theo turns his back, gets the wet shirt open in three quick moves, wrings a rope of water out onto the step. The hoodie drops over his head; the sleeves swallow his fingertips.
He drags the collar up over his nose and breathes in. His throat works once before he lifts his eyes to Nico.
...Smells like a bar rag. I'm keeping it.
letter: A letter? Now? I'm standing right here. Can't you say it to my face?
He doesn't open it. Folds it once, slides it into the pocket over his chest, and presses a hand flat over the wet cloth, like he's holding down something that wants to jump.
ring: A ring? ...Your bar does send-offs in style.
He doesn't hand it back. He slides it onto his little finger — a perfect fit — and turns it with his thumb, once, then again.
I'll hold onto it for you. Whenever I'm back, you'll get it.

skip: Theo hugs himself, shivering, teeth clicking, still forcing a smile. "Really. I'm fine."

en: Rowan wades down off the stairs, clipboard under one arm. One look at Theo's white lips and his brow knots; he unstraps the digital watch from his wrist.
Sports watch, it reads heart rate. When you're going hypothermic, it drops. Arm out. Let's check.
Wren hops off the last step, yanks the fitness band off Mason's wrist on her way past, and snaps it onto Nico's.
Control group. Nico, get closer — too far and it won't read right. I've got a hundred and fifty on it.
Fine, check it. ...Seventy-two. Steadier than any of you.

en.hint: The watch face reads 72. Wren wants you closer — five seconds, and every tap moves you an inch nearer to him. See if the number breaks the 150 she bet on.
win: The watch face throws cold light up under both their jaws. The number climbs and keeps climbing — even Rowan leans in for a second look — and stops at {bpm}.
{bpm}! Nico's only at {mine}! Theo, is that the cold?
Hypothermia makes it drop. I just said that.

Theo throws an arm over his face, ears glowing red. His other hand has a fistful of Nico's sleeve; it holds on two seconds longer, then lets go like it got burned. He strips the watch off and tosses it back to Rowan.
lose: The number hits {bpm} and Theo steps back in a splash, strips the watch off and tosses it back to Rowan.
Enough. I just hauled two cases of wine, any number's normal. Boxes.
Wren clicks her tongue and lobs the band back to Mason. "{bpm} isn't nothing, you know."
skip: I'm fine. Not now, Wren. After the boxes.

en.cap: Fri 11:24 PM · Ankle-deep in water, he looks back at you
en.prompt: Dim flooded bar basement at night, two men in their late twenties standing close in ankle-deep water holding boxes, flashlight, no text
then: Freeze! I'm keeping this one. For the wedding slideshow.

en: Rowan jerks his head at Wren. The two of them head upstairs single file, stomping the wooden steps extra loud, just so nobody down here can miss that they're gone.
Theo sits on an upturned empty crate, elbows on his knees, hair still dripping, water tracing his jawline down into his collar.
He stares at the black water. On his left wrist the old watch ticks forward, notch by notch, toward 7:10. For a long time he says nothing.
Nico. Seriously. Do you think I should go?

en.hint: He's waiting on one sentence from you. The tube light hisses over his head. Say the word and he might stay. That's exactly what scares you.

opts.t: Go. You waited five years for this. Don't stay for anybody.
then: Theo nods. A perfect smile, measured to the millimeter — a curtain-call smile, the kind that drops the second the lights go down.
opts.rthink: The contract's still unsigned; I've got the pen on me. One 'anybody' and he's crossed himself out too.

opts.t: Go. It's just... third row, aisle seat. It'll be empty now.
then: Theo's head snaps up, wet hair flinging a line of water, his eyes suddenly, frighteningly bright.
You sat there every show. Every single time, that's the first seat I looked for.
Once I found you, I could start.
Then he's the first to look away, wiping water off his face. "...Too many lines memorized. They just slip out."
opts.rthink: I've pulled the seating chart for every theater in New York. None of their aisle seats in row three come with him.

opts.t: Go. Finally nobody fighting me for my own tray.
then: Theo laughs. It doesn't reach his eyes. His thumb rubs back and forth over the watch face.
opts.rthink: I took that tray because only with empty hands would he sit down and drink with me. Five years, and he still hasn't figured it out.

en: Theo stands. One step forward, then another, black water rippling out from his boots. He stops a fist's width from Nico.
Close enough that Nico can see the water caught in his lashes, smell cold rain on him and the bitter orange and gin underneath. His throat bobs.

en.title: Blackout
en.txt: Snap. Every light dies at once. The pump coughs and chokes off. The whole building goes mute, and the dark pours in faster than the water.

en.why: Only each other in the dark

en: Nobody move! There's a power strip in the water!
I'm going up to kill the main. Till then, nobody touches the water.
The flashlight propped on a crate gets clipped by somebody's elbow and goes under with a heavy plunk. The light wobbles on the bottom like an eye closing — then nothing.
Nico's first move is to reach forward — Theo's a fist's width away, there's water underfoot, and live wire somewhere in it.
Dark so complete Nico can't see his own hand. Only the water, the muffled drumming of rain, and close by, someone's breath he can't quite hold steady.
A hand gets to Nico's wrist first. Cold. Wet. The palm rough, a thin ridge of callus across it.
It doesn't let go. It climbs slowly past the wrist bone and stops on the softest, thinnest skin on the inside of his forearm.
A thumb strokes once, right there. Just once. Nico's whole arm goes electric, every hair standing on end.
Someone's breath comes closer. Close enough to hear a swallow. That warmth lands right at the corner of his mouth.
Nico doesn't move. His pulse slams against his eardrums — thud, thud, thud. One thought surfaces: if the power comes back now, the first guy fried is probably him.

en.hint: In the dark, a rough hand rests on the inside of your forearm, thumb over your pulse. You can't see whose.

opts.t: ...Theo?
then: The hand doesn't leave. It tightens, all five fingers locking around his forearm, thumb pressed right over Nico's racing pulse.
opts.rthink: No hesitation; my name came first. Pitch black, and he knows my hand. So what exactly am I still scared of?

opts.t: Turn your hand over and lace your fingers through his, one by one.
then: In the dark his breath stutters, and his fingers clamp back hard, knuckles digging between Nico's. Heat gusts across Nico's face.
opts.rthink: He laced in. I've held hands on stage a hundred times. Never once with palms this wet.

opts.t: Who's there?
then: The hand freezes, fingertips drawing back like it's about to pull away. Then it stops, and settles back.
It's me. ...Who else did you think it would be?
opts.rthink: 'Who' nearly sent me back into the dark like none of it happened. But who else in here could find his wrist blind?

en.title: 47 Seconds in the Dark
en.teaser: What happened in the basement during those 47 seconds of blackout — only the two of you know.
then: In the dark, no one can see anyone. Only that hand, laced into Nico's fingers, tightening one by one, the palm slowly warming.
Theo's forehead comes to rest against his, wet hair brushing Nico's brow. His nose grazes the bridge of Nico's and stops an inch above his lips.
(so low only the two of them could hear) ...You know what I was thinking back in that aisle?
His breath is warm, bitter orange and gin. Nico eases back half an inch and his spine meets the cold steel shelving along the wall; one bottle ticks softly against another.
Nowhere left to back up to. So Nico stops backing up.
I was thinking — I wish the lights would go out.
His thumb slides from the inside of Nico's wrist down into his palm and draws a circle. Slowly. Slow like he wants Nico to remember it.
...And now they did. Call it a favor from upstairs?
Nico's lips graze something — rough stubble, or the warm corner of a mouth. He can't tell which.
Theo goes completely rigid, chest heaving, breathing in pieces — and doesn't give back a single inch.
Footsteps thud down the stairs. Before the hand lets go, it presses hard into Nico's palm, once, like a seal stamped there.
A second later Theo's voice is an arm's length off, steady as if nothing happened: "...Somebody fish out that flashlight?"

t: theo
Pitch black and he didn't pull away. I found his pulse — it was worse than mine. The itinerary in my pocket feels like a branding iron now.
wren
I'm right at the bottom of the stairs, can't see a thing, but I heard it — someone's breathing falling apart, and the recorder got every second. Long live the blackout.
rowan
I really didn't plan this one. Went up in the dark to kill the main, missed a step, nearly fed my clipboard to the water. ...Good work, universe.

en: Feet pound on the stairs. Rowan comes halfway down in the dark, breathing hard, a phone light skittering over the steps.
Rowan... did you plan the blackout too?
Somewhere in the dark, someone laughs low under his breath. The water's still rising. Nobody pays it any attention.
With the power gone, the Halfmoon was dark as the bottom of a lake. Rain hammered the windows in fistfuls, like someone flinging gravel at the glass.
Wren struck a match in the dark—a sharp hiss, the bite of sulfur. She worked her way down the bar, lighting stubby ones, fat ones, ones jammed into empty beer bottles.
The flames jumped. Wax crawled down the bottlenecks and set in milky tears. That low orange light softened every face—even Mason's iron jaw gave a little.
The six of them had felt their way up from the basement. The pump was dead; the water had stopped at the fifth step—not rising, not falling.
I can't fix the pump. No signal, and with this rain nobody's getting out.
Ethan limped to a stool and swung his bad leg up onto it, the skin puffing out around the brace. Mason reached to steady him; Ethan knocked the arm away.
It was one keg. I'll live.
The inside of Nico's forearm still held the heat of that hand. The patch of skin the thumb had stroked burned like a coin left on a stove.

then: Theo dropped onto the stool beside Nico; its legs scraped the floorboards. His soaked jeans had gone nearly black, plastered to his thighs.
He set his knee against Nico's and leaned in, slow, through two layers of wet denim, bone to bone, until the heat climbed up Nico's leg.
Down there you said the third-row seat would be empty from now on. ...I'm keeping that. We'll settle it later.
Theo sat two stools away, hunched, his big hands cupped over a candle. Light leaked between his fingers and turned his knuckles red.
Guess me leaving is just another bit to you.
else: Theo took the stool farthest from Nico. Back to the wall, long legs stretched out, boot heel grinding the floor, jaw set like the spine of a knife.
You said I should go. Fine. I'm listening.

en: Wren slapped an empty green bottle down on the bar—thunk. Her blazer hung off a chair back, shirtsleeves rolled to the elbows, two faded leather cords round her wrist.
Her thumb pressed the strip of black tape on the bottle's base, firm, a wicked little smile tucked into one corner of her mouth.
Rowan leaned on a pillar, work jacket half-zipped, radio still clipped to his chest. He shot her a wink—quick, and guilty as sin.
Sit here and wait for the rain? Power's out, party's not. Spin the bottle. Truth only.
Rules: whoever the neck points at answers. Whoever the base points at asks. Lie, and you kiss whoever's on your left.
Mason muttered "childish," but he didn't leave. He dragged his stool half a foot closer to the table instead—straight across from Ethan.

en.hint: That strip of tape on the bottom is crooked on purpose. In Wren's games, nothing ever just 'happens' to land.
win: First the hum of glass skidding on wood, then the candlelight flung off it in rings. Three spins. Slower. A wobble—and the neck stopped dead on Nico. The base pointed straight back at Wren.
Oh no. What are the odds. I'm asking.
Across the candles, Theo lifted his eyes. Flame danced in his pupils. He watched Nico without blinking, like a man watching someone who might bolt.

Across the candles, Theo lifted his eyes. Flame danced in his pupils. He watched Nico without blinking, like a man watching someone who might bolt.

en.q: When the lights died down in the basement—whose hand was on your arm in the dark?

en: Nico. When the lights died down in the basement—whose hand was on your arm in the dark?
Theo's glass froze halfway to his mouth. Condensation ran down over his fingers; he didn't notice. The veins on the back of his hand stood out, one by one.

en.hint: Pitch black down there; nobody saw a thing. But Wren was two steps away, and her recorder never went off.

opts.t: Couldn't see. Pitch black—could've been anyone.
then: Wren, in no hurry, clicked her recorder twice. Through the hiss, a man's voice, pitched very low: "...It's me."
Liar. Penalty. Whoever's on your left—
On Nico's left sat Mason, still holding a candle. His face darkened. "Don't even think about it." Rowan cleared his throat. "Make it a shot."
Theo said nothing. He poured one to the brim and pushed it over, the glass hitting the bar harder than it needed to. His jaw was set sharp enough to cut paper.
opts.rthink: Couldn't see. Sure. He heard me say 'it's me' clear as day. I filled it to the brim to see if he'd look at me while he drank.

opts.t: I know whose. I'm not answering.
then: Theo didn't join in. He watched Nico, throat working once, his knuckles going white around the glass.
...Rough hand, wasn't it. Funny what you remember.
Then he bent to fiddle with a candle wick, like someone else had said it.
opts.rthink: He knows, and he's covering for me. That's worse than an answer. I need something to do with my hands before I snap this wick.

opts.t: Theo. You answer that one. Whose?
then: Theo froze for a beat—then smiled. Mouth first, then the corners of his eyes. Candlelight caught the dark stubble along his jaw.
Mine. ...Dark like that, you grab whoever's standing steady.
He said it lightly. But that hand sat on his knee, thumb rubbing his own fingertips, as if it were still looking for that patch of skin.
opts.rthink: He threw it to me to see if I'd own it. I did. 'Somebody steady' was a lie—I could barely stand myself.

en: Nico gave the bottle the next spin. It didn't go as long; two wobbles—neck on Mason, base on Ethan.
Ethan's bad leg was still propped straight on the stool, the brace's velcro half open. He sat up, eyes locked across the table like he was about to dive for a shot.
My turn. Mason—before you went to the coach, did you think about me riding the bench for a whole season?
Mason had peeled off his soaked hoodie; the old jersey underneath strained across his shoulders. Head down, fists on his knees, squeezing tighter and tighter.

en.title: Mason Snaps
en.txt: Mason's fist slammed the table; every candle on it lurched. "I thought about it. One season on the bench beats you dragging that leg around at thirty. You wreck it, who's guarding the net behind me?"

en: Ethan just stared, mouth open, nothing coming out. The velcro slipped from his fingers with a loud rrrip that cut the silence clean through.
Mason's hand was still flat where it had landed, knuckles split and beading red. He wouldn't look at Ethan. His chest heaved like he'd just sprinted a full match.
Ethan said nothing. After a long moment he grabbed the dry towel off his stool and threw it; it hit the back of Mason's hand. He was still looking somewhere else.
Wipe that. Don't bleed on my stool.
Rowan caught Wren's eye and crooked two fingers, mouthing: One down. One to go.
Wren spun the third round. The neck wobbled to a stop on Theo; the base, once again, on her.
Fine. Dare: I play you a recording, and you don't grab it.
Wren thumbed the recorder on; the red light blinked. A few swipes of her nail, and she'd pulled up a file from five years ago.
Five years ago, Theo bombed a black-box show. After intermission people started leaving—folding seats flipping up one after another, clack, clack.
By curtain only one work light was still burning. And in all those seats, one person was left.

en.txt: One guy in the whole house — third row, on the aisle — clapping like he was a hundred people… Wherever I end up, I'm always coming back to drink at Nico's bar. That's a promise.
en.hint: Glasses clink in the background of the recording. Theo got drunk that night five years ago, and Wren's recorder was running.
then: Theo swore and lunged for it, half his weight crashing onto Nico's shoulder—rain smell and body heat landing all at once. Laughing, Wren held the recorder high over her head.
You grabbed. Dare's lost. —"Wherever I end up." I've been saving that for five years.
skip: Not listening? Fine. It's a family heirloom now.

en: Theo gave up. He was still braced on Nico's shoulder, forearm slung across his chest, looking at him from that close.
Close enough to see rain still caught in his lashes. His ears had gone scarlet, the flush running all the way down his neck.

en.hint: Five years. Every show he did, the third-row aisle seat was yours. He knew. Every time.

opts.t: Five years in that seat. You think I went for a theater with a busted heater?
then: ...Then what did you go for? Say it.
Theo's knuckles went white on the glass, the ice ticking against it. He waited.
Nico didn't say it. He picked up the tongs and snapped an ice cube clean in half.
opts.rthink: That night he left his program on the seat. I kept it—still pressed in my first script. If he says it plainly, I'll show him.

opts.t: Drunk promises don't count.
then: He said it fast, almost rough, like one second's delay and Nico would take it back.
...The bar tab part, I mean. I come back, I still pay.
opts.rthink: Sure, I was drunk. The line wasn't. I switched to bar tabs because I saw him starting to back away.

opts.t: Retreat behind the bar. "I need more ice."
then: Behind him, Wren let out a sigh heavy enough to bend the candle flames.
Theo watched him go and didn't follow. He set the glass down and ran his thumb around its rim, again and again.
opts.rthink: Hiding again. The ice bin's full; I checked. I count every time he ducks out. That's four tonight.

en: Wren hooked Theo's arm and hauled him toward the corner. "Mason's fist killed half the candles. Guest of honor—help me relight them."
Nico retreated behind the bar alone. Wax had dripped a trail of little white dots across the wood; he picked at one with a fingernail. It wouldn't come off.
Above the door the emergency light buzzed, washing everything a sickly green. He wiped his hands on his canvas apron—and his fingers hit a stiff corner in the pocket.
Under the Polaroid was a sticky note folded into a tight square, its edges gone soft with body heat. He hadn't put it there.
He unfolded it layer by layer. Pale yellow paper, every letter pressed in hard, one spot scribbled over and rewritten.
"N — five years of you remembering everyone's drink and everyone's birthday. Today it's my turn to remember you. Happy birthday. — T"
There was one more line on the back, scored through three times in ballpoint. Nico looked once, swallowed, and turned the paper back over.
The old clock on the wall gave a dry click. 12:00.
It was Nico's birthday. He hadn't told anyone. He'd nearly forgotten himself.
Five years of keeping this street's drinks and this street's tabs. First time anyone had kept one for him.
Nico stared at the T, and the corner of his mouth moved. Of course. The guy even had to pick up the tab on this.

en.hint: Midnight. Rain, candle smoke, a room full of noise. Nobody remembered your birthday—except him.

opts.t: When did he even slip this in…
then: Nico remembered that half-second when Theo squeezed past behind him, chest flat against his shoulder blades, hot as hell. He'd pressed so hard the T had dented the paper.
opts.rthink: When I slipped it in, my hand was shaking so bad I nearly missed the pocket. Don't flip it over. No—flip it.

opts.t: Read the front again, from the top.
then: "Today it's my turn to remember you." In five years, he was the only one who ever eased the tray out of Nico's hands.
opts.rthink: He's reading it twice. The front took me eleven drafts. The back I wrote once, then crossed out.

opts.t: …You idiot.
then: Barely a whisper; only Nico heard it. He pressed the note flat on the bar and held it there a long time, knuckles white.
opts.rthink: Too far to hear, but I can see his mouth move. Looks like swearing. Good. If he's cursing me, he got it.

t: theo
He found it. I'm in the corner lighting Wren's candles, two matches snapped already, and my eyes keep going to the bar.
rowan
Half a pad of sticky notes for those few lines. Theo, don't let them go to waste.
wren
His birthday? He forgot it himself. Only that idiot remembered. ...My eyes are stinging. It's the candle smoke. Doesn't count.

en: Rowan squeezed sideways behind the bar, his radio knocking the cabinet door. "Scoot. Ethan's knee is swelling up. Ice pack."
He crouched and yanked it open; cold air hit him in the face. Looking up, he saw the paper in Nico's hand. That right-leaning scrawl—he knew it.
Rowan glanced back. Theo was in the far corner, pinned down by Wren, lighting candles one by one—three matches before one caught. Out of earshot.
He made me swear not to tell you. But come daylight, he's on a plane.

en.title: Rowan's Secret
en.txt: "That five-year contract—he still hasn't signed a word of it."

en.why: He spent all night on that note

en: He was up all last night writing that. Went through half a pad. The rest of the job's yours.
Rowan left with the ice pack dripping a trail behind him. Passing Wren, their palms smacked together mid-air and split apart just as fast.
Across a room full of candles, Theo saw the paper in Nico's hand. He shoved the matchbox at Wren, pushed his sleeves up his forearms and came around the bar without a word.
He stopped behind Nico, bowed his head, and rested his forehead on Nico's shoulder. Heavy—like he'd finally let go of everything he'd held up all night.
Don't move. Just for a second.

then: His breath burned through Nico's T-shirt, right into his collarbone. He was still in Nico's gray hoodie, sleeves past his fingertips, the collar smelling of Nico's detergent.
else: His breath came through Nico's T-shirt, slow and scalding. His hair was still damp, the ends brushing cool along Nico's neck like a few stray drops of rain.

en: Through two layers of cotton Nico could feel Theo's heartbeat thudding into his back. Fast, ragged. Just like his own.

en.hint: His forehead is pressed to your shoulder, burning. Out past the bar, the whole room has stopped breathing.

opts.t: Bring a hand up to the back of his neck.
then: Theo went rigid, his back drawn tight as a strung bow. Then, bit by bit, he gave in, nose sinking into the curve of Nico's neck, breathing him in.
...Nico. Watch where you put that hand. I can't take it.
opts.rthink: One hand on my neck and the breath I held all night goes out of me. The seven-ten flight sounds like someone else's problem now.

opts.t: Just a second?
then: Theo lifted his head slowly, less than a fist from Nico's face. Candlelight swam in his eyes; his breath carried a trace of whiskey malt.
opts.rthink: 'Just a second' was my exit. He asked, and the exit's gone. Now I just want to see if he'll name a number.

opts.t: Don't move. Don't even breathe.
then: Theo laughed low; Nico felt it rumble through his back before the breath grazed his neck.
Holding your breath won't help. I can hear your heart right through your shirt.
opts.rthink: He won't even breathe, but his back hasn't shifted forward an inch. Five years his mouth runs; his body never once has.

t: theo
He didn't pull away. The breath I've been holding all night just went out of me, right there on his shoulder. ...Why the hell am I leaving.
rowan
Ice pack on Ethan's knee, turn around—yeah. My work here is done.
wren
Everyone's holding their breath. Whoever makes a sound right now goes in the flooded basement. By my hand.

en: Theo's eyes dropped to Nico's mouth and stayed there. His throat moved. Then again.
The note... you read the back too?

en.title: Against the Freezer
en.teaser: He lunges for the note—and the two of them crash into the freezer door.
then: Nico didn't answer. That was answer enough. Theo grabbed for it so fast the air moved and every candle on the bar leaned.
That line doesn't count. Mistake. Give it back.
Nico held it high. Theo crowded in, all six-foot-something of him, and they slammed back into the freezer door.
Cold seeping from the freezer at Nico's back, Theo's chest blazing against his front. One big hand braced beside Nico's ear, veins standing out across it, breathing hard.
Nico didn't let go. He jammed a knee against Theo's and held him off—not one more inch. Neither of them gave ground.
...Fine. Read it out loud and I'll take that as a yes.
Nico's lips parted. Theo's eyes dropped to them; his throat worked hard, his stubble almost scraping Nico's cheek.
He didn't back off. Forehead to Nico's forehead, their breath tangled, waiting.

en: He lifted a hand. His rough thumb dragged across Nico's lower lip, slow and barely there, like he was making sure—sure this wasn't another play.
He hooked a finger in Nico's apron strings and pulled. The canvas bit into Nico's waist; nose brushed nose.
Nico could smell the rain on him, and the bitter edge of lemon peel. One inch closer and—

en.prompt: Candlelit bar at midnight, two men forehead to forehead, almost kissing, no text

en: A huge crash from the basement, like a whole wall had given way. The floorboards shuddered underfoot.
A rack came down! Water's still at the fifth step—it's not coming up yet!
Theo jerked back half a step, finger still caught in the apron string, not letting go. His chest heaving, his eyes still glued to Nico's mouth.
Theo let go of the apron string, stepped out from behind the bar and headed for the stairs to check the water. Halfway there, he looked back.
The note was still crushed in Nico's palm. His sweat had bled a small ring around the T.

en.txt: That half step back at the freezer. I didn't want to take it. I was scared that if I didn't, I'd never get on that plane.

en: Unsent. The signal had only just crawled back to one bar. Three seconds later, a new one: Water's holding at the fifth step.

en.hint: He was right at the bottom of the stairs. Three rings — then he hung up himself.
lines: I'm at the bottom of the stairs. It's dark. Can't see your face. Makes this easier.
That line on the back of the note — I wrote it. I crossed it out, too.
If you saw it, pretend you didn't. ...If you didn't, don't go looking.
then: The line went dead. From the stairwell came the slosh of boots through water, one step, then another, coming up.
skip: Nico set the phone face down on the bar and didn't call back. From the stairwell came the slosh of boots through water, one step, then another, coming up.

ja: Friday, 10:40 p.m. A PRIVATE PARTY sign hangs on the Halfmoon's door, and thin rain slants across the brass crescent over it, blurring its glow.
Inside it's another world. A string of amber bulbs sags over the walnut bar, catching every old scratch, the brass rail worn bright by decades of elbows.
The air smells of juniper, bitter orange peel and wet wool coats. Ice slumps in every glass with a soft crack, like a sigh someone's been holding in.
Tonight is Theo's send-off. His flight to New York leaves at 7:10 a.m. The old clock behind the bar ticks louder than it ever has.
You're Nico, co-owner and bartender. White shirt cuffed to the forearm, black apron cinched tight, a little lemon juice still drying on your wrist bone.
You've made Theo's drinks for five years: one cube less ice, orange peel twisted twice, and the last pour before closing is always his. You could do it blind.
Some things haven't come up once in five years. Eight hours till boarding, and the bar spoon in your hand is rattling the ice far too hard.

Wren, swallowed by an oversized plaid blazer, flicks black-painted nails and slaps a silver recorder down mid-bar, next to her sticker-covered Polaroid. The red light blinks on like an eye that won't close. She arches a brow at Rowan by the door.
Rowan leans in the doorframe, black work jacket zipped to the chin, a pen tucked behind one ear, the digital watch on his wrist flickering through the seconds. He returns the look and types fast.
On the bar, Wren's phone lights up—
[Rowan: Plan A. Get them side by side. Don't let Nico hide behind the bar.]
Theo, middle seat. Closest to the bar. Faster refills.
Theo is standing by the empty stool dead center of the bar. Six-foot-something, a white T-shirt under a beat-up black leather jacket, the collar rain-damp and clinging to his collarbone.
Black jeans worn pale at the knee, rain still beaded on the heels of his Chelsea boots. A faded red string on his left wrist, pinned under an old watch with a fogged face.

He's folded his boarding itinerary into a tiny square and flips it through his long fingers. Jaw shaved clean, brow bone throwing a shadow, and when he grins, two fine lines crease at the corners of his eyes.
You're being so sweet tonight I'm starting to think it's a trap.
It is. Sit. It's your last night.
At opposite ends of the bar sit Mason and Ethan, four empty stools between them like a border neither will cross first.
Mason's shoulders strain a gray hoodie, sleeves shoved to the elbow, veins roping down his forearms. He grips a beer bottle, his thumb scraping at the label, again and again.
Ethan's ball cap is on backward, navy shell jacket still zipped, the brace on his right knee a hard ridge under his jeans. One big hand strangles his glass; his eyes stay nailed to the muted TV.
Day nine of the cold war. Their knees point at opposite walls. Neither has drifted an inch.
Theo leans across the bar, one long arm reaching, and eases the tray out of Nico's fingers inch by inch, setting it aside. His leather cuff drags over the wood, bringing a smell of rain and cedar.
His fingertips skim Nico's palm on the way out—rough, warm—and leave an itch that crawls from the palm all the way up the wrist.
Sit. Tonight's on me. You're a guest too.
Nico reaches to drag the tray back. Rowan's boot has already hooked out the stool beside Theo, Wren shoves from behind, and Nico lands in the seat with his apron still on.
Wren drops onto the stool on his other side and parks her chin on Nico's shoulder, her blazer smelling of smoke and peppermint. Her voice sinks to almost nothing but breath.
Year one, you'd tell him when he got back from tour. Year two, he had a boyfriend. Last year they broke up, and you said give him time.
Nico. You've been giving him time for five years.
Nico doesn't answer. He wrings the bar towel into a rope and shakes it out again. A no, he could take.

What he can't take is the recount: five years of drinks, five years of the last cigarette on the step after closing. Say it out loud and every one of them gets audited—until there isn't even a friendship left.
Theo leans over the bar and pulls the gin, the Campari and the sweet vermouth toward him one bottle at a time, measuring equal parts. He holds the jigger upside down once. The ratio is dead on.
Five years on this stool, watching you make a few hundred of these. He learned. He never said a word.
Theo slides the Negroni in front of you: garnet-red liquor swaying around a single ice sphere, a curl of orange peel on the rim. You reach for it and your fingers bump his.
Both hands lock around the same cold glass. Condensation runs down between your fingers.
He doesn't let go. His thumb, a little callused, presses into your knuckles and grinds across them one by one, slow enough to be deliberate. One second too long.
The veins on the back of his hand rise with the pressure, then sink. Your heartbeat drops with them, one heavy beat.
Under the bar, his knee presses into yours. Through his denim and your slacks, that one small patch burns like a glass fresh out of the washer.
In five years he's hooked an arm around your neck, smacked the back of your head, collapsed half his weight on your shoulder drunk. All of it inside the lines between buddies. This isn't.
You tell yourself the glass is slippery. The glass is not slippery.
Hands this cold. You been soaking them in the ice bin all night?

ja.hint: His hand is still on yours, his heat creeping in through your skin. Everyone's pretending not to look—Mason's bottle has stopped halfway to his mouth.

opts.t: It's the ice. Let go, you'll spill it.
then: Theo lets go—but first drags a fingertip down the ridges of your knuckles to the bone of your wrist, taking his sweet time.
opts.rthink: I practiced this pour all week with a soy sauce bottle. He tells me to let go, but his own hand hasn't moved an inch.

opts.t: Nico doesn't pull away. His pinky hooks back around Theo's.
then: Theo's throat works hard. His thumb strokes your knuckles twice, back and forth, harder the second time, before he lets go bit by bit.
Under the bar, Rowan's work boot catches Wren's ankle. Not hard. Not gently either.
Wren bites her straw flat, shoulders shaking, laughing so silently her eyes go wet.
opts.rthink: His pinky hooked back. Five years, and that's the first time. The itinerary in my pocket suddenly feels like somebody else's.

opts.t: Too cold for you? Then don't let go.
then: He doesn't. He clamps your whole hand in his palm and rubs it hard, twice, like working warmth into a frozen glove. Heat seeps in slowly between your fingers.
Then he lets go just like that and claps you on the shoulder. "There. Fit for work."
opts.rthink: He said don't let go and I almost took him at his word. That slap on the shoulder was for me. Three more seconds and I'd never leave.

t: theo
Hands straight out of the ice bin. I should've let go once he had the glass. My thumb wouldn't. Opening night, curtain up—my heart wasn't this loud.
wren
Two hands stacked on one glass, and they're the only two who think nobody's watching. Will my battery last until one of them cracks?
mason
Those two strike sparks just touching hands. Me and Ethan—nine days. Not even an 'excuse me.'

ja: Photo while we're all here! It's this episode's cover. Theo, Nico, together—closer. I could fit Rowan between you.
Just us? The rest of you aren't photogenic?
You two have co-hosted every party for five years and never taken one decent photo together. Stand still.

frames.prompt: two men standing stiffly side by side at a warm-lit wooden bar, one tall in a worn black leather jacket over a white t-shirt, the other a bartender in a white shirt with rolled sleeves and a black apron, both trying to look serious
same two men at the bar, the tall one in the leather jacket hooks an arm around the bartender's neck, both laughing, friends blurred in background
same two men at the bar mid-shove, the bartender elbowing the taller man in the ribs, both grinning, amber bulbs overhead

the bartender in a black apron grins and flips off the camera, the taller man in the black leather jacket is not looking at the lens, chin almost touching the bartender's hair, eyes lowered, looking at him

ja.hint: Wren shoves the Polaroid into Theo's hands and gives you a hard push in the small of the back. You slam into his chest—cold leather on top, a heavy heartbeat underneath. Four shots. No escape.
win: The flash pops four times, turning the bar into a stage. The prints slide out one by one, smelling faintly sour of developer.
The fourth one develops slowly: Nico flipping off the lens, grinning like an idiot. Theo isn't looking at the lens. His chin's almost in Nico's hair, eyes lowered. He's looking at Nico.
Wren pinches the fourth one between two fingers before anyone sees it, stuffs it into Nico's apron pocket, and pats it twice through the cloth.
This one's not making the cover. It's yours. Keep it.
Theo goes red to the ears and reaches straight for Nico's apron pocket. Rowan's arm swings out like a steel railing and blocks him.
